Controlled loading contrasts for m204, m120, and m181 test whether the observed loading effect transfers across alcohol and cyclic-acceptor environments. Condition curves for m173, m177, m125, m28, and m199 target the catalog regions where measured V2 errors were largest, while the chalcone and dibenzalacetone follow-ups separate the rejected onset analogy from any remaining finish response. Basic nitrogen rows cover quinoline-like, amino ester, and aminobenzonitrile environments. The remaining choices add low-similarity sulfoxide, phosphorus, nitro-alcohol, fused ether, polycarbonyl, and halogenated ether chemistry. This mix should improve structure-condition-loading transfer and endpoint-specific calibration across the Row-distribution rather than concentrating labels on one predicted outcome."}
